title: ApexFi V2 evaluation
protocol: Time-ordered split: first 75% of transactions to fit/validate, last 25% (147,635 rows, 5,100 frauds) as the untouched test block. Winners chosen on validation PR-AUC. A challenger replaces the incumbent only if it is at least 1% better.

decision.rule: switch only if >=1% validation PR-AUC gain

stage.model: Best ensemble: Voting: XGB + LightGBM + CatBoost

feature_sets.feature_set: F2: raw Gold columns only (no engineered)
F6: V2 full (adds card prior-mean amount)
F7: V2 full minus time-of-day features

retrained.split: random 70/15/15 of 1,225,601 labelled accounts (857,920 train / 183,840 validation / 183,841 test), 18 features, node_timestamp removed

operating_point.note: Weak by design of the data: published methods also score PR-AUC of only a few percent on DGraph-Fin. Use scores for ranking, not for automatic decisions.

dgraph.note: V1 DGraph-Fin numbers (ROC-AUC 0.938) came from node_timestamp, which exists only for fraud accounts. Without it the honest result is ROC-AUC 0.73-0.78 and PR-AUC 0.03-0.04.

limitations: IEEE-CIS is US card data in dollars, not UPI.
Benchmark models fit on a 100,000-row sample; the final model uses all 376,469 fit rows.
Most numbers come from one seed; run-to-run noise is about 0.004 PR-AUC.
GraphSAGE and the V1 stacker were not retrained in V2.
Money results depend on assumed review and friction costs.
Column M4 is empty in Gold (ETL defect, to be confirmed in Bronze).
